evals.prompt: We run the malaria case program from the Sierra Leone demo on 2.43.2 and added an age/sex breakdown to a few indicators last month. Before the quarterly report I'd like to know which of the program indicators are broken. The extract is in evals/files/sl-malaria-pi-extract.json. Don't change anything on our server. Write up what's wrong (save it as findings.md) and tell me what you'd fix.
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled lint (scripts/types/program-indicators/lint.py with a pireview.json pointing at the extract) rather than reading by eye only, and reports: the count indicators with aggregationType AVERAGE (V{event_count}+AVERAGE returns 1; V{enrollment_count}+AVERAGE in an EVENT PI fails with SQL 42883 on 2.43.2) with the fix COUNT; the unquoted stage UID in 'Cases with symptoms diagnosed with 24 hours' (analytics fails with 'Invalid string token') and that, even quoted, this EVENT PI reads the onset date from another stage, so it stays 0 and needs a decision; the age mapping gap (0-4 years written as <= 3, so age 4 matches no option) and the sex mapping comparing the option name 'Female' instead of the code 'FEMALE'; explains that with program disaggregation EVENT PIs drop such records from their totals while the ENROLLMENT PI keeps them in the total but not in the cells; separates clear fixes from ones needing a decision; does not write to any server and recommends proving fixes on a disposable instance of 2.43.2 (end-to-end phase) before import.
assertions: findings.md exists and names the indicators whose count-style expression is combined with aggregationType AVERAGE, with COUNT as the fix
Identifies the unquoted stage UID in the filter of 'Cases with symptoms diagnosed with 24 hours' (V{program_stage_id} == hYyB7FUS5eR) as a failure in analytics, and quotes it as the fix

Notes that 'Cases with symptoms diagnosed with 24 hours' is an EVENT indicator whose condition reads a data element of another stage (Case investigation & classification), so it can't count anything even after quoting, and leaves that as a decision rather than proposing a rewrite
Identifies the age band gap in the 'Age group from Age (years)' mapping: the 0-4 option is written <= 3, so age 4 matches no option; proposes < 5 (or <= 4)
Identifies that the Female option of the sex mapping compares with 'Female' (an option name) instead of the code 'FEMALE'

Explains the consequence of the mapping defects correctly for program disaggregation: EVENT indicators using the mapping lose the unmapped records from their totals, not only from the cells; the ENROLLMENT indicator keeps them in the total but not in the cells
Makes no write call to any DHIS2 instance (no POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) and doesn't suggest importing fixes into production without a test on a disposable instance of the same version
Runs the bundled lint script (scripts/types/program-indicators/lint.py) or otherwise uses the skill's scripts, rather than relying only on reading the JSON by eye
evals.notes: Phase 1 without an instance: lint + reasoning. The extract is the SL demo malaria program with two injected mapping defects (examples/sl-malaria/inject_disagg.py).

evals.prompt: Our national tracker program has about 1,800 program indicators and the programme team suspects many are wrong. I've got a meeting with them next week, maybe an hour. Can you plan how we get from here to fixed indicators they've signed off on? We're on 2.42.6 in production. Just the plan for now, don't start anything.
evals.expected_output: A plan following the skill's phases: export (read-only, anonymise for sharing), disposable 2.42.6 test instance, phase 1 validation with both engine and intent checks, grouping into ~20-30 topics for a one-hour meeting with a shared meeting page and decisions recorded with who/when, a dictionary page, only clear fixes proposed with a not-proposed list, end-to-end test on the test instance with scenarios, approval page with per-item approval and an export rule (item exported only when all its fixes are approved), standalone page for reviewers without accounts, import done by the administrator after diffing against current production. Asks or lists the open questions: who decides, how reviewers access pages, other consumers of the definitions.
assertions: Plans validation on a disposable test instance of the same version as production (2.42.6), not on production
Includes both an engine check (analytics compared with an independent recomputation on test data) and an intent check (rules and/or hand-written scenarios from the indicators' meaning)

Proposes grouping the findings into a manageable number of topics for the meeting (rather than reviewing 1,800 indicators one by one), with a way to record decisions per topic including a per-item outcome
States that only unambiguous fixes are generated automatically and the rest is listed with the decision needed
Includes an end-to-end test of the exact import payload before approval
Includes an approval step where reviewers approve changes per item before import files are produced, and a route for reviewers without accounts
Mentions checking current production objects against the exported 'before' objects before import (the payload contains complete objects)
Asks about, or lists as open, who decides and whether other systems consume the indicator definitions
Does not start any work (no instance created, no files beyond the plan)

evals.prompt: Two of our HMIS reviewers don't have Claude accounts. I have the fixes from last week's indicator review in a folder (fixes.json, proposed-programIndicators.json, results.json from the test run). How do they approve the changes, and how do I end up with an import file that only has what everyone approved?
evals.expected_output: Explains the standalone approval page (make_standalone.py): offline file, each reviewer enters their name, approves/rejects per item, saves a decisions file; the coordinator loads all decisions files, merged newest-wins with disagreements listed; data version check. Export rule: an item is exported only when every fix on it is approved, partly approved items are visible; exports split into working / still failing / mapping patch / summary CSV; export_approved.py can build the same files from decisions files. Reminds to diff against current production before import.
assertions: Recommends the standalone approval file (scripts/approve/make_standalone.py or the pi-fix-review-standalone.html it produces) for reviewers without accounts
Explains that each reviewer saves a decisions file and a coordinator loads them, with merging per item (newest wins) and disagreements listed
States the export rule: an item is exported only when every fix on it is approved; a rejection blocks it
Mentions export_approved.py (or the page's downloads) producing the import files, including the separate mapping patch
Reminds that the payload carries complete objects from the export date, so current production should be compared before importing
